target_customer: Consumers ordering convenience goods on DoorDash and Uber Eats, served by Cache-operated virtual stores
problem: Convenience delivery needs cheap local inventory; Cache used tiny automated dark stores that pass items to delivery drivers.
business_model: Retail margin on goods sold through delivery marketplaces from owned micro dark stores

founders.name: Christopher Wu
prior_employers: DoorDash (led business development for ghost kitchens)

founders.name: Jimmy Young
education: University of Sydney, computer science and chemical engineering
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; role title not stated there.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building automated dark store hardware, inventory handling and marketplace integrations with two people required robotics-adjacent engineering and operations.

defensibility.rationale: Distribution relied on third-party marketplaces and the hardware was unproven at scale, so there was little structural advantage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A dead-startups write-up says DoorDash's own DashMart competed, which that page's author argues; no founder statement confirms this.

market_need_then: Fast delivery boomed in 2020 and 2021 with heavy venture funding for dark stores; Cache received a Product Hunt newsletter feature on 9 August 2021.

branding.domain_note: grabcache.com, a verb plus name domain
branding.community_and_virality: A Product Hunt listing with 5 followers and a Trend Hunter feature; no community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A homophone of the common computing word cache and cash, hard to search for, and the consumer storefronts sat on DoorDash and Uber Eats under their own marketplaces.

outcome_analysis: Cache launched two small units in the Bay Area in 2022 after receiving a $125K YC investment, and a dead-startups write-up says it quietly wound down in 2022 without a formal announcement. That page's author infers an undercapitalized hardware model, a closed seed window as fast delivery funding collapsed and dependence on DoorDash and Uber Eats, but there is no founder post-mortem, so these factors are the archive's reconstruction. The only later confirmation is an October 2024 description of the CEO as a former YC founder.
notes: The $125K YC round rests on a dead-startups write-up whose citation numbers are inconsistent. The $9M seed dated 2024-03 rests on startupintros alone and conflicts with the same write-up and Crunchbase (pre-seed only); it is likely a different company named Cache or a data error, and is recorded only per the single-database rule. The shutdown year and failure factors rest on a secondary compilation. The grabcache.com site returned HTTP 503. Competitors left empty: DashMart, Gopuff, Jokr and Gorillas appear only in undated or 2022 and later articles; DashMart is noted in takeover_risk_then only.
